name: Struck-string physical-model synth controls that differ from subtractive synthesis: brightness set before the strike (not a filter), frequency-dependent decay (cutoff + slope) instead of sustain, strike point, harmonicity, three-string unison, and mallet-bounce retriggers at different note values per layer for sequenced polyrhythmic patches
goal: Design pads, basses and keys on a struck/plucked physical model and know which controls behave unlike a subtractive synth. Plucking brightness changes a sine-like tone into a saw-like one but only at the strike: lowering it while a note rings does nothing, so put a real filter after the model for sweeps. There is no sustain: decay and release plus a decay cutoff and slope define how partials above the cutoff die faster (low cutoff + high slope = more decay). Strike point acts like the pick position; harmonicity moves the tone from harmonic to inharmonic (steel-drum-like with more bloom); unison width detunes the three strings per note; smear softens transients. Mallet bounce makes a held note re-strike itself; stacking layers with different bounce values (dotted half, quarter, eight beats in the demo) gives sequenced, polyrhythmic patterns without a sequencer. Delta beyond our modal-partial skill: decay slope, pre-strike brightness and mallet-bounce layering.

source.title: Syngular: Pianoteq's New Physically Modeled Synth // Walkthrough & Demo
source.transcript_note: Product walkthrough with affiliate mention; licence and preset-tour content dropped.

prerequisites: Physical-model synth with struck-string/mallet engine, or Web Audio: Karplus/modal voice whose excitation lowpass is set per note, plus per-partial decay scaled above a cutoff (implementation note)
Post filter and EQ for sweeps

inputs.name: decay_cutoff
inputs.description: Frequency above which partials decay faster

inputs.name: decay_slope
inputs.description: How much faster partials above the cutoff decay

inputs.name: bounce_values
inputs.description: Mallet-bounce note values per layer, e.g. dotted half, quarter, 8 beats

constraints: Original synthesis recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any hybrid synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks or samples copied.
Pre-strike brightness cannot be modulated like a filter cutoff after the note starts. Use a post filter for sweeps.
No sustain stage: shape length with decay, release, the decay cutoff/slope and the sustain pedal.
Walkthrough of a licensed product; the editable parameters need a higher licence tier in that product. Affiliate and licence talk dropped. Preset names not copied.
Values were spoken as shapes (low/high), apart from the bounce note values. Set the rest by ear.

steps.action: Start from a sine-like init voice. Raise plucking/strike brightness to move toward a bright, saw-like tone. Test that turning it down while a note rings does not change that note.
steps.expect: Brightness changes only on the next strike

steps.action: Edit the harmonic profile (raise some partials, lower others) for a new basic colour, and set unison width to detune the three strings per note for synth-style thickness.
steps.expect: Thicker, chorus-like tone without a chorus effect

steps.action: Shape length: fast attack for keys or slower for pads; decay and release for ring time. Set the decay cutoff and slope: partials above the cutoff die faster as slope rises (low cutoff + high slope = shortest, darkest tail).
steps.expect: Short presses show faster high-frequency decay with a higher slope

steps.action: Set strike point (like pick position) and harmonicity (harmonic → inharmonic). With higher brightness and more bloom, inharmonic settings give steel-drum-like tones. Use smear to soften transients.
steps.expect: From pure tones to metallic drums

steps.action: Enable mallet bounce so a held note re-strikes; adjust bounce rate and decay over time.

Build a sequenced patch with 2–3 layers and different bounce note values (e.g. dotted half, quarter, 8 beats). Turning off bounce on one layer will not stop the pattern while the other layers still bounce.
steps.expect: Self-sequencing interlocking pattern from one held chord

steps.action: Map mod wheel → LFO rate, vibrato and tremolo depth. Finish with EQ and effects (chorus, phaser, delay, compression) and a post filter if you need cutoff sweeps.

verification: Changing brightness during a held note has no audible effect; the next note changes.
With a higher decay slope, high partials fade noticeably faster on a short press.
A held chord on the 3-layer bounce patch produces an interlocking rhythm.
Raising harmonicity away from harmonic produces an audibly inharmonic, metallic tone.
